messages.subject: Density Surface Mapping
parts:
Hello, I'm interested in trying density surface mapping, but things have =
advanced since Advanced Distance Sampling was first published - DSM is no=
w incorporated into Distance 6.0. Having not taken the advanced distance=
sampling workshop, I would like some hands-on experience before running =
through it with my own data. Is there a tutorial for the DSM engine avai=
lable that I can use? Is there any more up-to-date manual than the Advan=
ced Distance Sampling book? I haven't looked through the Distance help f=
iles in much detail yet, is that where I should start?

Also, on an unrelated note, is it possible to associate a g(0) multiplier=
with the observation layer instead of the global layer? I have differen=
t species with different g(0) multipliers. Does this mean that I need to=

make disparate Distance projects for each of them?

Thank you,
Philip Shirk

messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: Density Surface Mapping
parts:
Phillip:

There is a chapter in the users guide (11 I think) on the use of the DSM engine.
In addition, there is a sample project, dolphins.zip in the sample projects
directory. Have a look at those two sources, particularly working through the
sample project.

Distance still insists on having the multipliers at the global layer, not at
lower levels, I'm afraid.
